wfrp4e.rule.priest-aspect-change-retains.name: Priest aspect change retains known Miracles

wfrp4e.rule.priest-aspect-change-retains.cost_or_limit: The change is available at Priest level or higher and may reduce seniority.

wfrp4e.rule.rogue-downtime-complications.name: Rogue downtime complications

effect.summary: A rogue’s criminal livelihood can cause complications during certain downtime events or endeavours.

wfrp4e.rule.rogue-downtime-complications.cost_or_limit: Applies at the GM’s discretion to specified events
wfrp4e.rule.rogue-downtime-complications.go_wrong: May produce legal trouble, feuds, suspicion, or consequences for contacts
wfrp4e.rule.rogue-downtime-complications.combines: Accused Ally, Betrayed!, and Oi! You Spilled my Pint! events

wfrp4e.rule.contact-rescue-window.name: Contact rescue window

effect.summary: A player should have a chance to help a Contact before their fate is sealed.

wfrp4e.rule.contact-rescue-window.cost_or_limit: If not helped by the next downtime, the Contact’s fate may be sealed; three endeavours can help in the next period
wfrp4e.rule.contact-rescue-window.go_wrong: The Contact may suffer negative consequences
wfrp4e.rule.contact-rescue-window.blocked_reason: This is a procedural campaign rule.

wfrp4e.rule.random-business-income.name: Random business income

effect.summary: The table sets a business's trade, goods, earnings, and employer Intelligence.

wfrp4e.rule.random-business-income.cost_or_limit: Roll three times on the table before the embezzler steals.
wfrp4e.rule.random-business-income.combines: Goods may be taken instead of the rolled wealth.

wfrp4e.rule.fencing-recognition-modifier.name: Fencing recognition modifiers

effect.summary: Item value and time since theft modify a buyer's chance to identify stolen goods.

wfrp4e.rule.fencing-recognition-modifier.cost_or_limit: Uses the table's value and elapsed-time modifiers.
wfrp4e.rule.fencing-recognition-modifier.go_wrong: A buyer may recognize the goods as stolen.
wfrp4e.rule.fencing-recognition-modifier.combines: A successful removal of identifying marks applies a penalty to the buyer's test.

wfrp4e.rule.file-off-the-markings.name: File Off the Markings

effect.summary: A trade test can remove identifying marks and make recognition harder.

wfrp4e.rule.file-off-the-markings.cost_or_limit: A failed attempt can damage the item and expose its origin.
wfrp4e.rule.file-off-the-markings.go_wrong: The item's value can fall and its origin can be revealed.
wfrp4e.rule.file-off-the-markings.who_may: A character with an appropriate Trade skill.
wfrp4e.rule.file-off-the-markings.combines: Success gives the buyer a -2 SL penalty to Gossip or Evaluate.

wfrp4e.rule.safer-to-scrap-it.name: Safer to Scrap It

effect.summary: Precious metal or stone goods can be broken into components for sale.

wfrp4e.rule.safer-to-scrap-it.cost_or_limit: Success yields components worth half the item's value; failure yields a quarter.
wfrp4e.rule.safer-to-scrap-it.go_wrong: Failed work spoils the components' value.
wfrp4e.rule.safer-to-scrap-it.who_may: A character who succeeds at the required Trade test.
wfrp4e.rule.safer-to-scrap-it.combines: Components can be sold without risk of recognition.

wfrp4e.rule.take-a-trip.name: Take a Trip

effect.summary: Selling recognizable stolen goods elsewhere makes the buyer's Gossip test harder.

wfrp4e.rule.take-a-trip.cost_or_limit: Buyer suffers -3 SL to the Gossip test.
wfrp4e.rule.take-a-trip.who_may: A seller able to take the goods to another town or city.
wfrp4e.rule.take-a-trip.combines: Useful when news of a theft has not reached the destination.

wfrp4e.rule.plant-identities.name: Plant Identities

effect.summary: A character develops a false identity for an upcoming adventure.

wfrp4e.rule.plant-identities.cost_or_limit: A higher-status identity costs an entire Income Endeavour per status level; requires a Difficult Acting test.
wfrp4e.rule.plant-identities.go_wrong: A famous identity makes the test much harder.
wfrp4e.rule.plant-identities.combines: Success gives +2 SL on Charm and Performance and may grant Secret Identity.

wfrp4e.rule.whisper-campaign.name: Whisper Campaign

effect.summary: A successful rumour shifts a target's Status for a week.

wfrp4e.rule.whisper-campaign.cost_or_limit: Requires a Hard Charm test; each extra +2 SL adds a rumour detail.
wfrp4e.rule.whisper-campaign.go_wrong: Failure can reverse the intended Status change; a serious failure harms the speaker's reputation.
wfrp4e.rule.whisper-campaign.combines: The effect applies locally through the town.
wfrp4e.rule.whisper-campaign.mechanism: downtime test and temporary social status change

wfrp4e.rule.counterfeit-coins.name: Counterfeit Coins

effect.summary: A Forger can make up to fifty counterfeit coins after a day's work and a successful Trade test.

wfrp4e.rule.counterfeit-coins.cost_or_limit: Requires a currency-specific mould and a quarter ounce of base metal per coin.
wfrp4e.rule.counterfeit-coins.go_wrong: Failure produces visibly flawed coins that require an opposed Sleight of Hand test to pass unnoticed.
wfrp4e.rule.counterfeit-coins.who_may: A Forger with the needed tools and material.
wfrp4e.rule.counterfeit-coins.combines: Merchants refuse fakes they notice; repeat offenders may be reported.

wfrp4e.rule.gang-maintenance.name: Gang maintenance

effect.summary: A criminal organisation loses one level if its boss does not organise crime during a downtime period.

wfrp4e.rule.gang-maintenance.cost_or_limit: None beyond the stated downtime requirement.
wfrp4e.rule.gang-maintenance.go_wrong: The gang shrinks as members defect or a lieutenant challenges control.
wfrp4e.rule.gang-maintenance.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward level reduction tied to a missed upkeep action.

wfrp4e.rule.gang-location-restriction.name: Gang location restriction

effect.summary: A boss must be where the gang is based to undertake its gang-related endeavours; moving cities requires starting a new organisation.

wfrp4e.rule.gang-location-restriction.cost_or_limit: Gang actions are restricted to the organisation’s location.
wfrp4e.rule.gang-location-restriction.blocked_reason: The rule is a direct location restriction.

wfrp4e.rule.contact-development.name: Contact development

effect.summary: Contacts may change circumstances, location, health, relationships, or service quality as time passes.

wfrp4e.rule.contact-development.cost_or_limit: The GM checks the development table every three months and during downtime.
wfrp4e.rule.contact-development.go_wrong: Results may include arrest, illness, violence, or death.
wfrp4e.rule.contact-development.combines: The GM may disregard some negative outcomes if a character has helped the contact.
wfrp4e.rule.contact-development.blocked_reason: The rule is a scheduled update to a contact’s status.

wfrp4e.rule.gang-size-test.name: Gang size test

effect.summary: A successful Challenging Leadership Test grows a gang by one level; failure wastes the money and leaves its level unchanged.

wfrp4e.rule.gang-size-test.cost_or_limit: The boss pays the listed growth cost and must pass the test.
wfrp4e.rule.gang-size-test.go_wrong: Failure wastes the payment without increasing gang level.
wfrp4e.rule.gang-size-test.blocked_reason: The rule uses a basic success check and level change.

wfrp4e.rule.influence-cannot-oppose-the-.name: Influence cannot oppose the subject’s interests

effect.summary: A person pressured through gang influence cannot be made to act against their own interests.

wfrp4e.rule.influence-cannot-oppose-the-.cost_or_limit: The subject’s interests limit the action.
wfrp4e.rule.influence-cannot-oppose-the-.who_may: A person controlled through gang influence
wfrp4e.rule.influence-cannot-oppose-the-.blocked_reason: The rule is a straightforward restriction on what the influenced person will do.

wfrp4e.rule.contact-connection-cost.name: Contact connection cost

effect.summary: Establishing a Contact requires passing a Difficult Gossip Test and spending money equal to the Contact’s status.

wfrp4e.rule.contact-connection-cost.cost_or_limit: Test and status-based monetary payment are required.
wfrp4e.rule.contact-connection-cost.go_wrong: Failure means the connection is not made, though another endeavour can be tried.
wfrp4e.rule.contact-connection-cost.blocked_reason: The rule is a standard test and cost gate.

wfrp4e.rule.paying-your-dues.name: Paying Your Dues

effect.summary: Criminal members generally pay one status-based coin per gang level each month.

wfrp4e.rule.paying-your-dues.cost_or_limit: The example is a Brass 3 thief in a Level 3 gang paying three pennies monthly.
wfrp4e.rule.paying-your-dues.combines: Fee may also vary with activity, exposure, protection, and standing.

wfrp4e.rule.marking-your-territory.name: Marking Your Territory

effect.summary: Organisations coordinate criminal activity by territory to prevent overuse of targets and conflicts among members.

wfrp4e.rule.marking-your-territory.cost_or_limit: Larger organisations divide territory among underbosses and ringleaders.
wfrp4e.rule.marking-your-territory.go_wrong: Uncoordinated activity can provoke internal attacks or conflict.

wfrp4e.rule.protection-rackets.name: Protection Rackets

effect.summary: A payment protects a merchant only from the thieves who received it; gangs enforce paid premises as off-limits.

wfrp4e.rule.protection-rackets.cost_or_limit: Protection is limited to the paying thieves or organisation’s territory.
wfrp4e.rule.protection-rackets.go_wrong: Breaking the gang’s injunction brings harsh punishment.
wfrp4e.rule.protection-rackets.combines: Protection may be organised by a district-controlling gang.

wfrp4e.rule.luddataal-hereditary-title.name: Luddataal hereditary title

effect.summary: Talabheim’s ruler inherits a title granting a claimed divine right over the province and its people.

wfrp4e.rule.luddataal-hereditary-title.combines: When province and city unite, the ruler also bears Grátaal.

wfrp4e.rule.taalite-seasonal-holy-days.name: Taalite seasonal holy days

effect.summary: Taal’s holy days fall on equinoxes and solstices, with rites shared with other Old Gods.

wfrp4e.rule.taalite-seasonal-holy-days.cost_or_limit: Tied to the seasonal turning points.

wfrp4e.rule.pilgrimage-of-stones.name: Pilgrimage of Stones

effect.summary: Completing the pilgrimage and its strictures permanently grants Pure Soul.

wfrp4e.rule.pilgrimage-of-stones.cost_or_limit: Walk to twelve Talabecland holy sites without roads, rivers, or footwear; live by hunting and foraging, then sacrifice a deer or boar at the last site and bathe in its blood.
wfrp4e.rule.pilgrimage-of-stones.go_wrong: Failure to complete the requirements yields no stated reward.
wfrp4e.rule.pilgrimage-of-stones.who_may: Characters dedicated to proving devotion to Taal

wfrp4e.rule.zweig-act.name: Zweig Act

wfrp4e.rule.zweig-act.cost_or_limit: Applies in times of civil strife.

wfrp4e.rule.dwarfs-wizard-s-way-entry-la.name: Dwarfs’ Wizard’s Way entry law

wfrp4e.rule.dwarfs-wizard-s-way-entry-la.cost_or_limit: Applies on the fifth day monthly.

wfrp4e.rule.talabec-fish-law.name: Talabec fish law

wfrp4e.rule.talabec-fish-law.cost_or_limit: Nowadays enforced only against nuisance anglers.

wfrp4e.rule.hard-spirits-bill.cost_or_limit: One tankard or equivalent per person; one shilling per drink in tax.

wfrp4e.rule.watch-presence.name: Watch Presence

wfrp4e.rule.watch-presence.blocked_reason: This is game procedure rather than a world-mechanism rule.

wfrp4e.rule.local-justice-varies.name: Local justice varies

wfrp4e.rule.local-justice-varies.cost_or_limit: Outcomes depend on local tradition, accused persons’ social standing, offended parties’ status, and magistrates’ disposition.

wfrp4e.rule.outlaw-pardon-authority.name: Outlaw pardon authority

effect.summary: none stated

wfrp4e.rule.outlaw-pardon-authority.cost_or_limit: The Emperor may pardon citizens of Sigmar’s lands; Elector Counts may pardon outlaws in their provinces.

wfrp4e.rule.outlaw-recognition.name: Outlaw recognition

effect.summary: none stated

wfrp4e.rule.outlaw-recognition.cost_or_limit: On returning to the place of alleged crimes, an outlaw makes an opposed Challenging Stealth/Perception test each day; failure means recognition.
wfrp4e.rule.outlaw-recognition.go_wrong: Recognition may bring consequences decided by the GM.
wfrp4e.rule.outlaw-recognition.combines: Disguises and a new identity reduce recognition risk.

wfrp4e.rule.warrant-precedence.name: Warrant precedence

effect.summary: Imperial warrants outrank provincial ones; military and civil warrants usually rank lower, except the Imperial Military Court outranks provincial courts.

wfrp4e.rule.warrant-precedence.go_wrong: Competing arrest claims can put hunters at odds.
wfrp4e.rule.warrant-precedence.combines: Witch hunters may assert Imperial rank over bounty hunters.
wfrp4e.rule.warrant-precedence.blocked_reason: This is a legal priority rule that can be applied directly.

wfrp4e.rule.warrant-reward-conditions.name: Warrant reward conditions

effect.summary: A bounty is paid only when the warrant's stated conditions are met.

wfrp4e.rule.warrant-reward-conditions.cost_or_limit: The warrant may require a living or dead captive, or another specified service.
wfrp4e.rule.warrant-reward-conditions.go_wrong: Killing someone wanted alive can lead to a murder charge and harm the hunter's reputation.
wfrp4e.rule.warrant-reward-conditions.combines: Some contracts reward tracking or information instead of capture or killing.
wfrp4e.rule.warrant-reward-conditions.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward condition on payment.

wfrp4e.rule.proof-for-dead-outlaw-reward.name: Proof for dead-outlaw rewards

effect.summary: A dead outlaw's head must be identifiable; a destroyed body requires credible witnesses to the death.

wfrp4e.rule.proof-for-dead-outlaw-reward.cost_or_limit: Intact identifying features or credible witnesses are required.
wfrp4e.rule.proof-for-dead-outlaw-reward.go_wrong: Mutilation or destruction can prevent a reward claim.
wfrp4e.rule.proof-for-dead-outlaw-reward.combines: A sanctioned witch hunter's testimony can support a reward claim after the outlaw is burned.
wfrp4e.rule.proof-for-dead-outlaw-reward.blocked_reason: The rule is an evidence threshold for a reward.

wfrp4e.rule.anyone-may-take-a-bounty-con.name: Anyone may take a bounty contract

effect.summary: The Empire requires neither a licence nor guild membership to take a bounty contract.

wfrp4e.rule.anyone-may-take-a-bounty-con.cost_or_limit: Established professionals are more likely to win bids.
wfrp4e.rule.anyone-may-take-a-bounty-con.combines: Some cities restrict who may claim general-poster bounties.
wfrp4e.rule.anyone-may-take-a-bounty-con.blocked_reason: This is a direct eligibility rule.

wfrp4e.rule.warrant-arrest-authority.name: Warrant arrest authority

effect.summary: A warrant can be issued privately to a specific hunter or posted publicly; general warrants can be claimed by anyone.

wfrp4e.rule.warrant-arrest-authority.cost_or_limit: Capturing or killing the wrong person under a general warrant is illegal.
wfrp4e.rule.warrant-arrest-authority.go_wrong: An unlawful killing can result in a murder charge.
wfrp4e.rule.warrant-arrest-authority.who_may: The warrant's named hunter or, for public general warrants, anyone
wfrp4e.rule.warrant-arrest-authority.combines: Some cities reserve general-poster claims to guild members.
wfrp4e.rule.warrant-arrest-authority.blocked_reason: This is an ordinary legal authorization rule.

wfrp4e.rule.thief-taker-warrant-restrict.name: Thief-taker warrant restriction

effect.summary: Apprehending thieves without a warrant is technically illegal; the expected procedure is to report them to the Watch.

wfrp4e.rule.thief-taker-warrant-restrict.cost_or_limit: A thief-taker's early work focuses on recovering stolen property.
wfrp4e.rule.thief-taker-warrant-restrict.go_wrong: Attempting an arrest without authority may itself be unlawful.
wfrp4e.rule.thief-taker-warrant-restrict.combines: A client may hire a thief-taker to retrieve property.
wfrp4e.rule.thief-taker-warrant-restrict.blocked_reason: This rule concerns legal authority, not an effect in the basic grammar.

wfrp4e.rule.guild-city-bounty-restrictio.name: Guild-city bounty restriction

effect.summary: In cities with bounty hunter guilds, independents may bid for warrants, but only guild members may claim general-poster bounties.

wfrp4e.rule.guild-city-bounty-restrictio.cost_or_limit: Membership is required for general-poster claims in those cities.
wfrp4e.rule.guild-city-bounty-restrictio.go_wrong: Illegal arrest can be charged as assault or kidnapping; illegal killing as murder.
wfrp4e.rule.guild-city-bounty-restrictio.who_may: Guild members for general-poster claims; independents may bid for warrants
wfrp4e.rule.guild-city-bounty-restrictio.combines: Guilds may revoke membership for killing innocents.
wfrp4e.rule.guild-city-bounty-restrictio.blocked_reason: This is a direct legal restriction.

wfrp4e.rule.general-bounty-identificatio.name: General bounty identification

effect.summary: A bounty hunter guild may revoke membership from a hunter who kills innocents.

wfrp4e.rule.general-bounty-identificatio.combines: Guilds generally do not take part in murder trials.
wfrp4e.rule.general-bounty-identificatio.blocked_reason: This is a direct organisational rule.

wfrp4e.rule.mountain-sickness.name: Mountain Sickness

effect.summary: At high altitude, a failed Endurance test causes immediate nausea and malaise until exposure ends or a successful test is made.

wfrp4e.rule.mountain-sickness.cost_or_limit: Characters make a Challenging Endurance test; accustomed Ogres, Dwarfs, and animals are exempt.
wfrp4e.rule.mountain-sickness.go_wrong: A failed test causes the sickness.
wfrp4e.rule.mountain-sickness.combines: Exposure ends the condition, or a successful test does.
wfrp4e.rule.mountain-sickness.blocked_reason: The condition and its duration can be resolved directly.

wfrp4e.rule.swamp-fever.name: Swamp Fever

effect.summary: Bites can transmit a disease with a raw red bite patch, fever and other symptoms.

wfrp4e.rule.swamp-fever.cost_or_limit: Requires a bite; incubation is 1d5 days and it lasts 1d10 days.
wfrp4e.rule.swamp-fever.where_from: Bites from creatures such as bog leeches and sea slugs
wfrp4e.rule.swamp-fever.blocked_reason: The disease’s stated symptoms and timing can be represented with basic effects.

wfrp4e.rule.waystone-channelling.name: Waystone channelling

effect.summary: Elven waystones channel excess magical energy toward the Great Vortex at Ulthuan’s centre.

wfrp4e.rule.waystone-channelling.go_wrong: The energy coursing through the stones can be dangerous.
wfrp4e.rule.waystone-channelling.combines: The magical energy may be associated with different Lores.
wfrp4e.rule.waystone-channelling.blocked_reason: The passage describes a flow of magical energy that can be represented with the basic effect grammar.

wfrp4e.rule.hunting-ownership-law.name: Hunting ownership law

effect.summary: Under Imperial law, wild beasts belong to the owner of the land they occupy.

wfrp4e.rule.hunting-ownership-law.cost_or_limit: Hunting another owner’s game is treated like taking food from their store.
wfrp4e.rule.hunting-ownership-law.go_wrong: Poachers hunt unlawfully and may face conflict with gamekeepers.
wfrp4e.rule.hunting-ownership-law.blocked_reason: The ownership restriction can be applied as a game rule.

wfrp4e.rule.foul-air.name: Foul Air

effect.summary: Suffocating gas impairs those crossing it and can kill an unconscious victim.

wfrp4e.rule.foul-air.cost_or_limit: A pocket spans 2d10 yards; a victim who passes out dies in TB rounds without rescue.
wfrp4e.rule.foul-air.go_wrong: Exposure causes impairment, unconsciousness or death.
wfrp4e.rule.foul-air.combines: Resilience may be spent to escape; tests after leaving end the effects.
wfrp4e.rule.foul-air.blocked_reason: The described impairment and lethal timer can be handled as game effects.

wfrp4e.rule.waystone-lore-bonus.name: Waystone Lore bonus

effect.summary: Waystones grant nearby spellcasters a bonus when casting with the Lore they channel.

wfrp4e.rule.waystone-lore-bonus.cost_or_limit: The bonus applies within 20 yards and only to relevant Lores.
wfrp4e.rule.waystone-lore-bonus.combines: Uses the Lore associated with the particular stone.
wfrp4e.rule.waystone-lore-bonus.blocked_reason: The continuing radius-based modifier requires an area-field capability.

wfrp4e.rule.ogham-lore-bonus.name: Ogham Lore bonus

effect.summary: Nearby Life or Hedgecraft casters receive improved casting and channelling results.

wfrp4e.rule.ogham-lore-bonus.cost_or_limit: Applies within 20 yards and only to the specified Lores.
wfrp4e.rule.ogham-lore-bonus.combines: Lore of Life and Lore of Hedgecraft
wfrp4e.rule.ogham-lore-bonus.blocked_reason: The continuing radius-based modifier requires an area-field capability.

wfrp4e.rule.game-prices-change.name: Game prices change

effect.summary: The value of game varies with season and buyer suspicion that it was obtained illegally.

wfrp4e.rule.game-prices-change.cost_or_limit: Prices depend on season and perceived illegality

wfrp4e.rule.hound-hunting-trait-training.name: Hound hunting-trait training

effect.summary: Teaching a dog a hunting trait takes an hour and a Difficult (-10) Animal Training Test; failure requires a day’s rest before retrying.

wfrp4e.rule.hound-hunting-trait-training.cost_or_limit: One hour and a Difficult (-10) test per attempt
wfrp4e.rule.hound-hunting-trait-training.go_wrong: Failure means a day of rest before trying again
wfrp4e.rule.hound-hunting-trait-training.combines: A hound with a hunting trait can assist a Hunting Endeavour

wfrp4e.rule.hawk-hunting-trait-training.name: Hawk hunting-trait training

effect.summary: Teaching a hawk a hunting trait takes three hours and a Hard (-20) Animal Training Test; failure requires a day’s rest before retrying.

wfrp4e.rule.hawk-hunting-trait-training.cost_or_limit: Three hours and a Hard (-20) test per attempt
wfrp4e.rule.hawk-hunting-trait-training.go_wrong: Failure means a day of rest before trying again
wfrp4e.rule.hawk-hunting-trait-training.combines: A suitably trained hawk can assist a Hunting Endeavour

wfrp4e.rule.hunting-endeavour-assistance.name: Hunting Endeavour assistance

effect.summary: A suitably trained hunting hound or hawk can assist an Outdoor Survival test for a hunt.

wfrp4e.rule.hunting-endeavour-assistance.cost_or_limit: Animal must have at least one listed hunting trait
wfrp4e.rule.hunting-endeavour-assistance.combines: Hounds or hawks may provide assistance

wfrp4e.rule.edicts.name: edicts

effect.summary: Knights must defend the Empire, oppose Chaos-marked bearers, serve superiors, and stay loyal to allies.

wfrp4e.rule.edicts.combines: Some chapters modify the oaths for local circumstances.
wfrp4e.rule.edicts.blocked_reason: This is a playable obligation rather than a special effect.

wfrp4e.rule.bond-of-mutual-support.name: bond of mutual support

effect.summary: The Middenheim chapter and the Todbringer family support one another.

wfrp4e.rule.bond-of-mutual-support.cost_or_limit: Applies to the named chapter and family.
wfrp4e.rule.bond-of-mutual-support.who_may: The Middenheim chapter and ruling Todbringer family.
wfrp4e.rule.bond-of-mutual-support.combines: A local modification to the order’s oaths.
wfrp4e.rule.bond-of-mutual-support.blocked_reason: The compact is a straightforward lasting relationship.

wfrp4e.rule.sartosan-firm-rule.name: Sartosan firm rule

effect.summary: Sartosan captains must not attack ships guarded by other Sartosan captains.

wfrp4e.rule.sartosan-firm-rule.cost_or_limit: The rule protects business between captains.
wfrp4e.rule.sartosan-firm-rule.go_wrong: Breaking it can lead to capture and punishment by fellow captains.

wfrp4e.rule.licence-to-recruit.name: licence to recruit

effect.summary: Recruiters in the Empire need local permission to hire armed men; higher authorities grant broader territorial coverage.

wfrp4e.rule.licence-to-recruit.cost_or_limit: A province-wide writ requires the Elector Count’s court and is expensive.
wfrp4e.rule.licence-to-recruit.go_wrong: Corruption can enable abuse of licences.
wfrp4e.rule.licence-to-recruit.combines: A licence governs recruitment and operations in the issuing ruler’s territory.
wfrp4e.rule.licence-to-recruit.blocked_reason: This is a direct permission and territorial limit.

wfrp4e.rule.pirate-law.name: Pirate law

effect.summary: Sartosa forbids theft and executes murderers, thieves, swindlers, and traitors.

wfrp4e.rule.pirate-law.combines: Pirate Captains elect a supreme authority.
wfrp4e.rule.pirate-law.blocked_reason: The law is an ordinary prohibition with a stated penalty.

wfrp4e.rule.wound-loss.name: Wound loss

effect.summary: Damage removes Wounds after Toughness Bonus and Armour Points reduce it.

wfrp4e.rule.wound-loss.cost_or_limit: Each damage point removes one Wound; Toughness Bonus and armour reduce damage.
wfrp4e.rule.wound-loss.go_wrong: At zero Wounds, further injury can cause Critical Damage.
wfrp4e.rule.wound-loss.combines: Toughness Bonus and Armour Points reduce damage.

wfrp4e.rule.critical-wounds.name: Critical Wounds

effect.summary: A successful double on an attack can cause Critical Damage before the target reaches zero Wounds; damage at zero Wounds causes it automatically.

wfrp4e.rule.critical-wounds.cost_or_limit: A blow causes no more than one Critical Wound; extra Wounds from a critical result do not trigger another roll.
wfrp4e.rule.critical-wounds.go_wrong: Critical injuries can debilitate or kill.
wfrp4e.rule.critical-wounds.combines: Critical Damage table and hit location.

wfrp4e.rule.bleeding-condition.name: Bleeding Condition

effect.summary: Bleeding removes a Wound at each round's end, with special effects at zero Wounds and while unconscious.

wfrp4e.rule.bleeding-condition.cost_or_limit: At zero Wounds, stop Wound loss and test Endurance each turn; unconscious bleeding characters risk death each round.
wfrp4e.rule.bleeding-condition.go_wrong: Unconscious bleeding characters have a ten-percent-per-condition death chance; a double reduces bleeding by one condition.
wfrp4e.rule.bleeding-condition.combines: Heal tests or healing spells and prayers can remove conditions; full removal causes Fatigued.

wfrp4e.rule.pulling-your-blows.name: Pulling Your Blows

effect.summary: A declared restrained attack suppresses most Critical Damage and removes several weapon qualities.

wfrp4e.rule.pulling-your-blows.cost_or_limit: Declare before attacking; critical damage occurs only if the target reaches zero Wounds; unavailable with ablaze-causing weapons, missiles, or spells.
wfrp4e.rule.pulling-your-blows.who_may: An attacker choosing to subdue a target.
wfrp4e.rule.pulling-your-blows.combines: Hack, Impact, Impale, and Penetrating are lost.

wfrp4e.rule.death.name: Death

effect.summary: A character may die from a critical result, accumulated critical injuries while unconscious at zero Wounds, or a foe's execution.

wfrp4e.rule.death.cost_or_limit: Unconscious characters at zero Wounds die at round's end if critical results exceed Toughness Bonus, unless a critical wound is healed.
wfrp4e.rule.death.who_may: Characters meeting the stated injury conditions; enemies may execute an unconscious character with an Action and suitable weapon.
wfrp4e.rule.death.combines: Healing a Critical Wound can prevent death from accumulated injuries.

effect.summary: A critical result marked T causes no extra Wounds and does not count toward death from critical injuries.

wfrp4e.rule.sudden-death.name: Sudden Death

effect.summary: At zero Wounds, the GM may simply declare an NPC dead or unconscious.

wfrp4e.rule.sudden-death.cost_or_limit: Not for player characters or NPCs with Luck Talent.
wfrp4e.rule.sudden-death.who_may: GM adjudication for suitable background NPCs.

wfrp4e.rule.mounted-movement-and-actions.name: Mounted movement and actions

effect.summary: A rider can spend their Move to direct a mount’s movement and an Action to direct its action.

wfrp4e.rule.mounted-movement-and-actions.cost_or_limit: A mount needs at least Trained (Mount) to count as a mount.
wfrp4e.rule.mounted-movement-and-actions.go_wrong: Untrained mounts may require a test to follow directions.
wfrp4e.rule.mounted-movement-and-actions.combines: Roughrider permits directing an action without a test or action.
wfrp4e.rule.mounted-movement-and-actions.blocked_reason: This is a procedural rule rather than a special effect.

wfrp4e.rule.mount-attacks.name: Mount attacks

effect.summary: War-trained mounts can act as combatants; Skittishness and training affect their target choices.

wfrp4e.rule.mount-attacks.cost_or_limit: Untrained-for-war mounts are preoccupied with their rider’s orders.
wfrp4e.rule.mount-attacks.go_wrong: Accidents can occur when a mount chooses targets.
wfrp4e.rule.mount-attacks.combines: The mount’s Skittish and Trained (War) traits determine behaviour.
wfrp4e.rule.mount-attacks.blocked_reason: This is a creature-control and combat procedure.

wfrp4e.rule.quadruped-hit-locations.name: Quadruped hit locations

effect.summary: A roll table determines which body part of a four-legged animal is hit.

wfrp4e.rule.quadruped-hit-locations.cost_or_limit: Uses the listed roll bands for head, body, and legs.
wfrp4e.rule.quadruped-hit-locations.blocked_reason: This is a game procedure, not a world mechanism.

wfrp4e.rule.falling-from-a-mount.name: Falling from a Mount

effect.summary: A fall usually counts as two yards and causes 1d10+6 damage reduced by Toughness Bonus, not armour.

wfrp4e.rule.falling-from-a-mount.cost_or_limit: Large or larger mounts add one yard per size step.
wfrp4e.rule.falling-from-a-mount.combines: A mount may test Initiative to notice a rider’s fall.
wfrp4e.rule.falling-from-a-mount.blocked_reason: A damage calculation is expressible as an ordinary harm effect.

wfrp4e.rule.death-unconsciousness-and-pr.name: Death, Unconsciousness and Prone

effect.summary: A dead, unconscious, or prone rider falls; the same states in a mount throw off its rider.

wfrp4e.rule.death-unconsciousness-and-pr.cost_or_limit: Special equipment can prevent a rider falling in the stated circumstances.
wfrp4e.rule.death-unconsciousness-and-pr.go_wrong: The rider is thrown off when the condition occurs.
wfrp4e.rule.death-unconsciousness-and-pr.combines: The rider and mount’s conditions affect their relationship.
wfrp4e.rule.death-unconsciousness-and-pr.blocked_reason: This is a direct conditional movement rule.

wfrp4e.rule.mount-care.name: Mount care

effect.summary: Neglected required care makes a mount test Toughness each day; failure may cause fatigue and later illness or other problems.

wfrp4e.rule.mount-care.cost_or_limit: A person can care for about six animals in adverse conditions or twelve with a stocked stable.
wfrp4e.rule.mount-care.go_wrong: Disease, damaged shoes, parasites, or escape may follow neglect.
wfrp4e.rule.mount-care.combines: Requires Animal Care when conditions demand it.
wfrp4e.rule.mount-care.blocked_reason: This is a direct upkeep rule.

wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-breaking.name: Demigryph breaking

effect.summary: A rider who stays mounted for a day and night can earn a Demigryph’s acceptance.

wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-breaking.cost_or_limit: The attempt is often fatal; only the breaker may ride that beast.
wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-breaking.go_wrong: The beast may throw the rider or tear them apart.
wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-breaking.mind: The creature relents after the ordeal.
wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-breaking.who_may: The person who breaks the Demigryph
wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-breaking.where_from: Demigryphs of the Empire’s deep forests
wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-breaking.combines: The beast gains Trained (Broken), and adult trained beasts also have Mount, War, Magic, and Shock Cavalry.
wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-breaking.blocked_reason: The lasting exclusive rider relationship requires a creature-binding capability.

wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-upkeep-and-breedin.name: Demigryph upkeep and breeding

effect.summary: Demigryphs need fresh meat, costly custom tack, and cannot currently be bred in captivity.

wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-upkeep-and-breedin.cost_or_limit: Two GC of fresh meat weekly; tack costs twice a horse’s; captive breeding has failed.
wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-upkeep-and-breedin.mind: They are difficult to breed and sex.
wfrp4e.rule.demigryph-upkeep-and-breedin.blocked_reason: These are direct economic and biological constraints.

wfrp4e.rule.crewed-weapon-requirements.name: Crewed weapon requirements

effect.summary: Crewed weapons require suitably trained operators; insufficient crews impose reload, accuracy, or flaw penalties, and a misfire affects the whole crew.

wfrp4e.rule.crewed-weapon-requirements.cost_or_limit: Reduced crews incur cumulative penalties; an unqualified crew member does not count.
wfrp4e.rule.crewed-weapon-requirements.go_wrong: A misfire affects every crew member.
wfrp4e.rule.crewed-weapon-requirements.who_may: Characters with the relevant Ranged skill
wfrp4e.rule.crewed-weapon-requirements.combines: Crew members may assist with reload-time tests.
wfrp4e.rule.crewed-weapon-requirements.blocked_reason: Crew size and weapon penalties can be handled as game rules.

wfrp4e.rule.salvo-quality.name: Salvo Quality

effect.summary: A salvo weapon can fire repeatedly, spending one Salvo point per shot and requiring a reload at zero.

wfrp4e.rule.salvo-quality.cost_or_limit: Each later shot in the same turn takes a cumulative −10 Ranged penalty.
wfrp4e.rule.salvo-quality.go_wrong: A misfire triggers the Salvo Artillery Misfire Table.
wfrp4e.rule.salvo-quality.who_may: Users of a weapon with Salvo
wfrp4e.rule.salvo-quality.combines: Uses the weapon’s Salvo rating and misfire rules.
wfrp4e.rule.salvo-quality.blocked_reason: This is a straightforward use limit with a reload condition.

wfrp4e.rule.salvo-artillery-misfire-tabl.name: Salvo Artillery Misfire Table

effect.summary: A misfire can injure the crew, destroy the artillery piece, or send shots in random directions.

wfrp4e.rule.salvo-artillery-misfire-tabl.cost_or_limit: The result depends on a D10 roll and remaining Salvo points.
wfrp4e.rule.salvo-artillery-misfire-tabl.go_wrong: Crew injuries and possible destruction of the weapon; on the highest result, stray missiles may strike nearby characters.
wfrp4e.rule.salvo-artillery-misfire-tabl.combines: Triggered by a Salvo weapon misfire.
wfrp4e.rule.salvo-artillery-misfire-tabl.blocked_reason: The variable damage, destruction, and random-direction attacks need rules beyond the basic effect grammar.

wfrp4e.rule.breaking-from-combat.name: Breaking from Combat

effect.summary: A combatant can disengage by spending Advantage, succeeding at Dodge, or fleeing.

wfrp4e.rule.breaking-from-combat.cost_or_limit: Each method has different tests, movement, and possible penalties.
wfrp4e.rule.breaking-from-combat.go_wrong: A failed Dodge pins the character; fleeing may invite a free attack and cause Broken.
wfrp4e.rule.breaking-from-combat.blocked_reason: The procedure uses ordinary movement and test outcomes.

wfrp4e.rule.pursuits.name: Pursuits

effect.summary: Chasers and quarry make movement tests to alter their separation until the quarry is caught or escapes.

wfrp4e.rule.pursuits.cost_or_limit: Distance starts between 0 and 10; 0 means caught and 10 means escaped.
wfrp4e.rule.pursuits.go_wrong: A captured quarry may have to sacrifice a slow member or confront the pursuers.
wfrp4e.rule.pursuits.combines: Movement tests use Athletics, Ride, or Drive as appropriate.
wfrp4e.rule.pursuits.blocked_reason: The rule tracks distance and test results.

wfrp4e.rule.complex-pursuits.name: Complex Pursuits

effect.summary: Tracks each participant’s pursuit distance individually, with progress determined by movement tests and circumstances.

wfrp4e.rule.complex-pursuits.cost_or_limit: Distance is measured in ten-yard increments; movement 3 or lower makes foot tests harder.
wfrp4e.rule.complex-pursuits.go_wrong: Poor test results can halt or cause a fall and Prone.
wfrp4e.rule.complex-pursuits.combines: Uses individual distances, movement rates, environments, and pursuit tests.
wfrp4e.rule.complex-pursuits.blocked_reason: The rule is implemented through movement, distance, and test results.

wfrp4e.rule.impeded-movement.name: Impeded Movement

effect.summary: A Prone or Entangled participant loses their next chance to make pursuit progress while freeing themselves.

wfrp4e.rule.impeded-movement.cost_or_limit: Costs the participant their next pursuit test opportunity.
wfrp4e.rule.impeded-movement.go_wrong: They may need a test to free themselves.
wfrp4e.rule.impeded-movement.who_may: Participants in a pursuit who cannot move freely
wfrp4e.rule.impeded-movement.combines: Triggered by Prone, Entangled, or another movement restriction.
wfrp4e.rule.impeded-movement.blocked_reason: This is a direct movement restriction.

wfrp4e.rule.obstacles.name: Obstacles

effect.summary: A stationary obstacle blocks a participant when the pursuit distance to it reaches zero, forcing them to stop or navigate it.

wfrp4e.rule.obstacles.cost_or_limit: The GM sets perception and navigation tests and failure consequences.
wfrp4e.rule.obstacles.go_wrong: Failed tests can cause conditions, injury, delays, or other listed setbacks.
wfrp4e.rule.obstacles.combines: Obstacles can be created by the quarry using a Perception test and an Athletics test.
wfrp4e.rule.obstacles.blocked_reason: This is a test-gated movement obstacle.

wfrp4e.rule.exhaustion.name: Exhaustion

effect.summary: Repeated pursuit running requires Endurance tests; failure gives Fatigued.

wfrp4e.rule.exhaustion.cost_or_limit: Typical tests occur every ten foot rounds, twenty mounted rounds, or thirty vehicle rounds, with the GM adjusting as needed.
wfrp4e.rule.exhaustion.go_wrong: Failure fatigues the participant or their mount or draft animals.
wfrp4e.rule.exhaustion.combines: A Fatigued animal may slow unless persuaded to continue with Charm Animal.
wfrp4e.rule.exhaustion.blocked_reason: This is a threshold-based test and condition.

wfrp4e.rule.group-advantage.name: Group Advantage

effect.summary: Advantage is pooled separately for allies and adversaries rather than tracked per character.

wfrp4e.rule.group-advantage.cost_or_limit: Characters add to the Ally pool; hostile or neutral NPCs add to the Adversary pool.
wfrp4e.rule.group-advantage.go_wrong: At round’s end, advantage can shift from the suppressed pool to the dominant one.
wfrp4e.rule.group-advantage.who_may: Characters and NPCs in a conflict
wfrp4e.rule.group-advantage.combines: Changes how Advantage is gained, spent, and lost.
wfrp4e.rule.group-advantage.blocked_reason: The rule is a shared counter with specified transfers.

wfrp4e.rule.advantage-pool-dominance.name: Advantage Pool Dominance

effect.summary: At the end of a round, one Advantage moves from the suppressed side’s pool to the dominant side’s pool, or is created if the suppressed pool is empty.

wfrp4e.rule.advantage-pool-dominance.cost_or_limit: Dominance is decided by combatant numbers or tactical position.
wfrp4e.rule.advantage-pool-dominance.go_wrong: The losing side’s pool is depleted by the transfer.
wfrp4e.rule.advantage-pool-dominance.combines: Uses Ally and Adversary Advantage Pools.
wfrp4e.rule.advantage-pool-dominance.blocked_reason: This is a simple resource transfer.

wfrp4e.rule.initial-advantage.name: Initial Advantage

effect.summary: The GM may seed an Advantage pool for a side’s initial tactical benefits.

wfrp4e.rule.initial-advantage.cost_or_limit: Only the highest modifier in each circumstance is awarded; circumstance values include movement, numbers, surprise, terrain, and threats.
wfrp4e.rule.initial-advantage.who_may: Sides at the start of combat
wfrp4e.rule.initial-advantage.combines: Awarded to the pool of the side benefiting from the circumstance.
